questions.q: Exports of goods are $900m and imports of goods are $1,200m. What is the balance in goods ($m)? Include the sign.
questions.hint: Include the minus sign if negative.
questions.fb: Balance = exports − imports = 900 − 1,200 = −300, a deficit. See 'Calculating the balances'.

questions.q: Exports of services are $160m and imports of services are $100m. What is the services balance ($m)?
questions.fb: Services balance = exports − imports = 160 − 100 = 60, a surplus. See 'Calculating the balances'.

questions.q: Goods and services balance −$240m, primary income +$70m, secondary income +$45m. What is the current account balance ($m)?
questions.hint: Include the minus sign if negative.
questions.fb: Current account = goods and services + primary income + secondary income = −240 + 70 + 45 = −125, a deficit. Keep the sign.

questions.q: A current account deficit is $50m and GDP is $1,000m. The deficit is what percentage of GDP?
questions.fb: Percentage of GDP = deficit ÷ GDP × 100 = 5. Always judge the size of a deficit relative to the economy.

questions.q: Workers' remittances sent home are recorded in:
questions.fb: Transfers with nothing received in exchange, such as aid and remittances, are secondary income. See 'The four parts of the current account'.

questions.q: Profits, interest and dividends from abroad are recorded in:
questions.fb: Income from investment and work abroad is primary income. See 'The four parts of the current account'.

questions.q: Complete: exports are recorded in the balance of payments as a ________.
questions.fb: Money coming in is a credit (+) and money going out is a debit (−). See 'The big idea'.

questions.q: Which of these is likely to be a CYCLICAL cause of a current account deficit?
opts: A boom at home that raises imports
questions.fb: A growing domestic economy raises imports and is short term and often self-correcting. The others are structural. See 'Causes of a current account deficit'.
questions.model: A boom at home that raises imports

questions.q: Which is likely to be a STRUCTURAL cause of a deficit?
opts: A short-term slowdown among trading partners
A temporary rise in home spending
A one-off fall in oil prices
questions.fb: Structural causes are long term and not self-correcting, such as poor competitiveness, an overvalued exchange rate or low productivity. See 'Causes of a current account deficit'.

opts: The value of imports is greater than the value of exports
The quantity of imports is greater than the quantity of exports
questions.fb: A deficit compares values, not quantities. This is a common exam error. See the 'Do not write this' box.
questions.model: The value of imports is greater than the value of exports
